newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan 14-day NCDs average yield at 5.904 pct.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan 14-day NCDs average yield at 5.904 pct.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank issued T$5 billion in 14-day negotiable certificates of deposit on Wednesday at an average yield of 5.904 percent, a central bank official said.
The range of the bids was between 5.749 and 5.970 percent.

The NCDs issue came just two days after central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong on Monday pledged that the bank would take the economy's health into consideration in any further issues of the short-term instruments.
"We will not continue to blindly issue NCDs," Sheu said in the wake of the stock market's plunge on Monday. "We will do it in consideration of overall economic conditions."
The central bank had made major daily NCD issues almost every day up until March 21, reportedly trying to curb the loose liquidity that many analysts said was fuelling a stock market rally.
The last such intervention came on March 21, the same day the stock market plunged more than three percent over a hog foot and mouth epidemic sweeping the island.
The stock market fell dramatically on Monday and Tuesday over the pork crisis, but rebounded strongly on Wednesday.
